brief.headline: Cut prices to Mars Plastics levels and save ₹16.09 L a year — we're paying 19.6% more on our biggest bottle SKU

priceAsk.summary: Match Mars Plastics on bottles and caps across the board
priceAsk.target: ₹1.38/NOS on the 30 ML white HDPE bottle (currently ₹1.65) and ₹0.81/NOS on the 28 mm PP cap (currently ₹0.90) — saving ₹16.09 L per year
priceAsk.basis: Mars Plastics already gives us these prices for identical items; the 30 ML bottle alone costs us ₹11.74 L extra per year at Premier's price, and the market ask for the 28 mm cap sits at ₹0.85–0.95 typical (Premier is ₹0.90, room to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume), so ₹0.81 is fair and proven

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days after receipt to 30 days, then explore 15 days in six months
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹10.63 L cash freed up for us at 30 days; another ₹5.31 L at 15 days

brief.financialLeverage: Premier Plastic publishes no financials, so we can't see their revenue, profit or how tight cash is for them. Our ₹1.29 Cr annual spend is meaningful but we have no percentage to quote. Because their finances aren't public, the plan leans on our own purchase data and lining up a strong second source. We should push firmly on price — Mars already proves the numbers work — and use faster payment as a sweetener only if they move to ₹1.38 and ₹0.81.

evidence.point: We pay Premier ₹1.65 per piece for the 30 ML white HDPE bottle; Mars Plastics charges ₹1.38 for the same item
evidence.figure: ₹1.65/NOS vs ₹1.38/NOS, gap 19.6%, costing us ₹11.74 L extra per year

evidence.point: The 28 mm PP induction-wad cap costs us ₹0.90 at Premier vs ₹0.81 at Mars
evidence.figure: ₹0.90/NOS vs ₹0.81/NOS, gap 11.1%, costing us ₹4.23 L extra per year

evidence.point: Total extra cost across all rigid plastic packaging SKUs from Premier
evidence.figure: ₹16.09 L per year vs the best prices we already pay

evidence.point: Open market ask for the 28 mm cap sits at ₹0.55–1.20 per piece, typically ₹0.85–0.95, with room down to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume
evidence.figure: Market verdict: MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec

evidence.point: Faster payment frees up working cash: 30 days saves us ₹10.63 L, another 15 days on top saves ₹5.31 L
evidence.figure: ₹10.63 L at 30 days, ₹5.31 L at 15 days more

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — does pharma bottles, caps and preforms, top second-source candidate and already approved for packaging

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) for pails, containers and pharma — strong, profitable, robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited
alternates.why: Manufacturer lead to qualify (verify before RFQ) — pan-India, medium confidence; not yet priced or audited but a potential maker-direct source

risks: Premier publishes no financials, so we can't gauge their stability or how hard to squeeze — watch for signs of distress (delivery slips, quality drift) and keep Manjushree warm as backup
Mars Plastics proves ₹1.38 and ₹0.81 are real prices, but if Premier refuses to match we need to shift volume fast — qualify Manjushree and Mold-Tek now so the threat is credible
Offering faster payment (30 or 15 days) costs us ₹10.63 L to ₹15.94 L in tied-up cash — only give it in exchange for the full ₹16.09 L price cut, not as a standalone concession
The 60 ML bottle gap is tiny (₹2.25 vs ₹2.20, only ₹10670/year) — don't spend negotiating energy there; focus on the 30 ML bottle and the cap where the real money sits
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We've been comparing notes across suppliers, and Mars Plastics is giving us ₹1.38 on the 30 ML bottle and ₹0.81 on the 28 mm cap — that's ₹16 lakh a year less than your prices, so let's talk about how we close that gap.
